봉영여중 영어B 추가지문 - 2학년
주제찾기
1 7번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Many animals use tricks to get what they want, but the large blue butterfly is one of the cleverest. Its life starts when the mother lays small white eggs on wildflowers. The baby caterpillars hatch and eat the flower heads. Later, they drop to the ground and wait for a new home. When red ants come near, the caterpillars give off a smell just like a baby ant’s. The ants are fooled and carry the caterpillars into their nest. There, the ants feed and protect them like their own babies. In the end, the caterpillars become butterflies and fly away, leaving the ants with nothing.
①how a butterfly tricks ants into raising its young
②why red ants carry food into their nests
③the best flowers for butterflies to lay eggs on
④how ants protect their queen from enemies
⑤the dangers caterpillars face in the wild
2 8번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Everyone needs some personal space around them. When someone comes too close, people often feel uncomfortable. However, the amount of space people want depends on their culture. In the U.S., people usually keep about one meter away from others in line. In Russia, people are used to standing much closer, even just a few inches behind someone. The COVID-19 pandemic changed these habits for a while. During that time, people everywhere kept their distance from others. Today, people tend to adjust their distance depending on the situation.
①the history of coffee shops in the U.S.
②how to use a self-order kiosk safely
③how culture and situations affect personal space
④why Russian people like crowded places
⑤the health problems caused by the pandemic

봉영여중 영어B 추가지문 - 2학년
주제찾기
3 9번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Scientists once put a barracuda, a violent fish, into a tank with some mackerel. As expected, the hungry barracuda attacked the small fish. Then the scientists placed a glass panel between them. The barracuda kept hitting the glass, but it could not reach the mackerel. After bumping its nose many times, it finally gave up. Even after the glass was removed, it stopped where the barrier used to be. Many people act the same way after they fail. Their fear of failure stops them from growing, even though failure can lead to success.
①how scientists catch large fish in the sea
②why barracudas are dangerous to people
③the best way to build a large aquarium
④how mackerel escape from bigger fish
⑤how the fear of failure can stop our growth
4 10번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Mr. A and Mr. B got stuck in traffic and reached the airport thirty minutes late. Mr. A learns that his flight left on time. Mr. B learns that his flight was delayed and left only five minutes ago. Most people think that Mr. B will feel much worse. He keeps thinking, “If only we had taken another street.” A tiny change could have saved his flight. When we miss a goal by a lot, we rarely imagine a different result. But when we miss it by a little, it hurts more, and we keep replaying the “what ifs.”
①how to avoid traffic jams on the way to the airport
②why missing something by a little feels worse
③the reasons flights are often delayed
④how surveys are used to study people
⑤why limousines are popular at airports

봉영여중 영어B 추가지문 - 2학년
주제찾기
5 11번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Chilean Patagonia is one of the most beautiful and wild places on Earth. It has deep fjords, huge glaciers, and mountains that nobody has explored yet. Strong winds, icy rivers, and thick forests make it very hard to travel there. This land is home to the Wenger Patagonian Expedition Race. Fifty-six adventurers from around the world come to test themselves there. For ten days, the teams fight against changing weather and rough land. Fourteen teams start the race, but fewer than half of them finish. That is why it is called the ultimate eco-endurance challenge.
①the history of mountain climbing in Chile
②how glaciers are formed over many years
③why people should protect wild animals
④a tough race held in the wild land of Patagonia
⑤how to choose good team members for a trip

봉영여중 영어B 추가지문 - 2학년
요지찾기
6 7번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
The large blue is a European butterfly with a surprising way of growing up. Its caterpillars do not stay on the flowers for long. They fall to the ground and wait for red ants to find them. By changing their shape and smelling like baby ants, they trick the ants. The ants take them home and care for them as if they were their own young. The caterpillars live like kings and queens inside the nest. After they turn into butterflies, they simply fly away. The poor ants are left with an empty nest, as if they were waking from a dream.
①개미는 다른 곤충과 협력하여 둥지를 짓는다.
②라지 블루 나비는 개미를 속여 자신의 새끼를 기르게 한다.
③애벌레는 꽃을 먹어야만 나비가 될 수 있다.
④붉은 개미는 애벌레를 잡아먹으려고 둥지로 옮긴다.
⑤나비는 다른 동물을 속이지 않고 스스로 살아간다.
7 8번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
How close we stand to others is not the same everywhere. Americans in a coffee shop line usually leave about one meter of space. Standing too close to a kiosk can even feel like a threat to their privacy. In Russia, however, people stand closer, and standing far back may look strange. Then the pandemic made people all over the world avoid standing close. Even after it ended, it left a mark on how people think about distance. Now people stand close at concerts but far apart in libraries. Personal space changes with culture and with the situation.
①셀프 주문 키오스크는 사생활을 지켜 주는 기계이다.
②러시아 사람들은 미국 사람들보다 예의가 없다.
③팬데믹이 끝난 뒤 사람들은 예전 습관으로 완전히 돌아갔다.
④개인 공간의 크기는 문화와 상황에 따라 달라진다.
⑤공공장소에서는 항상 1미터 이상 떨어져 서야 한다.

봉영여중 영어B 추가지문 - 2학년
요지찾기
8 9번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
A barracuda is a large fish known for its violent behavior. In an experiment, it tried again and again to attack some mackerel behind a glass panel. Each time, it only bumped its nose and failed. At last, it quit trying. Later, the glass was taken away, but the barracuda still would not swim past that spot. It believed the barrier was still there. Like the barracuda, people often stop trying after they fail. But failure is often a step toward success, so we should not let fear limit us.
①실패에 대한 두려움 때문에 시도를 멈추면 성장할 수 없다.
②과학 실험에 동물을 이용해서는 안 된다.
③위험한 일은 처음부터 시도하지 않는 것이 좋다.
④장벽이 사라지면 누구나 다시 도전한다.
⑤포식성 물고기는 먹이를 쉽게 포기하지 않는다.
9 10번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Two men missed their flights after a traffic jam. One flight had left on time, but the other had left just five minutes earlier. In a survey, 96 percent of people said the second man would be more upset. This is because he can easily imagine how things could have been different. A different street or a shorter stop might have changed everything. When we fail by a wide margin, such thoughts do not come easily. But a near miss stings, because success was so close. The closer we are to success, the more we think about what might have been.
①비행기를 놓치지 않으려면 일찍 출발해야 한다.
②설문 조사의 결과는 항상 믿을 만하다.
③성공에 가까이 갔다가 실패할수록 더 큰 아쉬움을 느낀다.
④큰 차이로 실패할수록 더 오래 후회하게 된다.
⑤교통 체증은 사람들을 가장 화나게 하는 일이다.

Fifty-six adventurers in fourteen teams compete for ten days. The weather changes all the time, and the land is rough and dangerous. Some teams even get lost and have no idea where they are. The race pushes every team to the edge of exhaustion. In the end, fewer than half of the teams reach the finish line. It is truly one of the toughest races on the planet.
